extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_short: criteria for morphisms and ampleness on curves
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of cohomological, numerical, and geometric criteria and theorems used to decide when morphisms are closed embeddings, when line bundles are base-point-free/very ample/amplе, and when higher direct images/cohomology vanish or behave well; primarily aimed at studying projective curves and projective/proper morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber versus pushforward cohomology map (base change map)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural morphism (Riπ_* F) ⊗ κ(q) → Hi(π^{-1}(q), F|_{π^{-1}(q)}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ﬁber of the pushforward may not equal the cohomology of the fiber, but there is always this natural map; in good situations (Cohomology and Base Change Theorem 26.1.6) this map is an isomorphism. See Exercise 18.7.B(a) and the Leray spectral sequence for the origin of such maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection formula (general form)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicompact separated morphism π: X → Y and quasicoherent sheaves F on X and G on Y, there is a natural morphism (Riπ_* F) ⊗ G → Riπ_*(F ⊗ π^* G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the map using the FHHF theorem (Exercise 1.6.I). If G is locally free then this natural morphism is an isomorphism (Exercise 18.7.E(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative dimensional cohomology vanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a projective morphism and Y is locally Noetherian (or O_Y coherent over itself), then the higher pushforwards Riπ_*F vanish in degrees higher than the maximum dimension of the fibers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The projectivity hypothesis is necessary (counterexample given in 18.7.6). The statement is local on Y; proof uses affine covers of fibers and afffine cover cohomology vanishing (Property (vi) of §18.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Serre vanishing (π-ample twist kills higher pushforwards)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes and L is π-ample, then for any coherent F on X there exists m0 such that for m ≫ 0, Riπ_*(F ⊗ L^{⊗ m}) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes Serre vanishing to the relative/proper setting (cf. Theorem 18.1.3(II)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's cohomological criterion for ampleness
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian, X proper over A, and invertible sheaf L on X, L is ample iff for all coherent F there exists n0 so that for n ≥ n0, Hi(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗ n}) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an equivalent cohomological characterization of ampleness under Noetherian hypotheses (Theorem 18.8.1). Use Serre vanishing and Riemann–Roch type inputs in proofs; (a–c) in Theorem 16.2.2 are equivalent to (e) here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's cohomological characterization of affineness
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasicompact quasiseparated scheme X is affine iff for any quasicoherent sheaf F on X, Hi(X, F) = 0 for all i > 0 (equivalently: for any quasicoherent ideal sheaf I, H^1(X, I) = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The direction from (c) to (a) contains the real substance; proofs are classical (Theorem 18.8.6). Analogue: Stein spaces in complex analytic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck's Coherence Theorem (proper→coherent pushforwards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a proper morphism of locally Noetherian schemes. For any coherent sheaf F on X, Riπ_* F is a coherent sheaf on Y for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case i=0 is standard; proof uses Chow's Lemma and the Leray spectral sequence. This theorem lets one extend projective arguments to proper morphisms (Theorem 18.9.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chow's Lemma (approximation by projective birational morphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Spec A is proper with A Noetherian, there exists a projective surjective µ: X' → X that is an isomorphism on a dense open subset (so X' is projective over Spec A and µ is birational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce statements about proper schemes to projective ones. Various versions and generalizations exist; see 18.9.2 and following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for a projective morphism to be a closed embedding (Theorem 19.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is algebraically closed and π: X → Y is projective, finite type k-schemes, injective on closed points, and injective on tangent vectors at closed points, then π is a closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projectivity and algebraically closed base are necessary (counterexamples given). The tangent injectivity condition is equivalent to 'unramified' in finite-type schemes over algebraically closed fields (Exercise 21.6.I). The theorem is reduced to the finite morphism criterion of Theorem 19.1.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphism degree 0/1 criterion for closed embedding (Theorem 19.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite between Noetherian schemes and the degree at every point of Y is either 0 or 1, then π is a closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: π is injective on points and induces isomorphisms on residue fields at points in the image; Nakayama's lemma used to check surjectivity on rings in affine local reduction (proof 19.1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivity plus finite fibers implies finite morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A projective morphism with finite (dimension 0) fibers is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the reduction of Theorem 19.1.1 to Theorem 19.1.2: finiteness of fibers follows from upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension and projectivity (see 19.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity on tangent vectors forces degree ≤ 1 at closed points
rubrics_metrics.description: If a projective morphism is injective on tangent vectors at closed points, then the degree of the morphism at closed points is at most 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use classification of finite morphisms to Spec k and properties of tangent maps (Exercise 19.1.D). Degree is upper semicontinuous, so once ≤1 on closed points it holds everywhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre duality for curves
rubrics_metrics.description: For a geometrically irreducible regular genus g curve C over k with canonical ω_C, for any coherent sheaf F on C, hi(C, F) = h^{1−i}(C, ω_C ⊗ F^∨) (duality between H^0 and H^1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular ω_C has degree 2g−2 and g sections. Use Serre duality to convert statements about low-degree line bundles into high-degree cohomological statements (Remark 19.2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: No nonzero sections for negative-degree line bundles on curves
rubrics_metrics.description: If deg L < 0 on a projective curve C, then h0(C, L) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: deg L counts zeros minus poles of rational sections; a regular (pole-free) section would force nonnegative degree (Remark 19.2.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree 0 line bundles: h0 is 0 or 1 and characterization of triviality
rubrics_metrics.description: If deg L = 0 then h0(C, L) is either 0 or 1; h0(C, L) = 1 iff L ≅ O_C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonzero section of degree 0 line bundle has neither zeros nor poles, hence gives trivialization (Remark 19.2.4). Geometric integrality used to ensure h0(O)=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-degree line bundle dimension formula (Riemann–Roch consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If deg L > 2g − 2 on a genus g curve C, then h0(C, L) = deg L − g + 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows by Serre duality and Riemann–Roch (Remark 19.2.5). Useful for determining dimensions of complete linear series for large degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twist-by-point changes h0 by at most 1
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed point p of degree 1, h0(C, L) − h0(C, L(−p)) is either 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short exact sequence 0 → L(−p) → L → L|_p → 0 shows H0(L|_p) = 1 and gives the bound (Remark 19.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-point-freeness criterion via h0 drop at points
rubrics_metrics.description: If for every closed point p (degree 1) h0(C, L) − h0(C, L(−p)) = 1, then L is base-point-free (hence induces a morphism to projective space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality shows for each p there exists a section not vanishing at p, so there are no base points (Remark 19.2.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separating points criterion for linear series
rubrics_metrics.description: If for distinct closed points p and q, h0(C, L) − h0(C, L(−p − q)) = 2, then the linear series separates p and q (i.e., the map to projective space sends p and q to distinct points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently there is a section vanishing at q but not at p (Remark 19.2.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separating tangent vectors criterion (local separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If for a closed point p of degree 1, h0(C, L) − h0(C, L(−2p)) = 2, then the morphism given by L separates tangent vectors at p (cotangent map surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition yields a section vanishing to order exactly 1 at p but not order 2, giving nonzero differential on pullback (Remark 19.2.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Very ampleness criterion via pairwise h0 drops
rubrics_metrics.description: If for all closed points p and q (not necessarily distinct) h0(C, L) − h0(C, L(−p − q)) = 2, then L gives a closed embedding into projective space (separates points and tangent vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the separating points and tangent vectors criteria with Theorem 19.1.1 to conclude very ampleness (Remark 19.2.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical degree criteria for base-point-freeness and very ampleness on curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Over an algebraically closed field, if deg L ≥ 2g then L is base-point-free; if deg L ≥ 2g + 1 then L is very ample (and the associated global sections give a closed embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are standard numerical sufficient conditions (Remark 19.2.11). They follow from the previous separation and dimension-counting remarks and Riemann–Roch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness on projective regular integral curves equals positive degree
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on a projective, regular, integral curve over a field k is ample iff deg L > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a simple numerical criterion for ampleness on curves (Exercise 19.2.C); can be extended to non-algebraically closed fields by base change arguments (Exercise 19.2.D).
